en:
In any case... I am really dreading the moment I walk
through my front door. I cannot see it going well.

Well, my wife was hoping I'd get promoted, and I know she's
only gonna get disappointed...

How am I even supposed to look her in the eye, let alone
explain to her what happened?
Even so, I think you should tell her the truth.
But she'll be furious! I just know it!
Look, you two are married. Your wife should love you for who you are, not what your job is. I'm sure that's already the case.
Besides, what you did today took a lot of courage. At least give yourself credit for that.
Huh... You know what, maybe you're right! Guess it couldn't hurt to tell my better half the truth every now and then, eh?
(Seems like he's in a much better mood now.)
Do you really need to tell her everything?
I mean, this is just a work thing, so I doubt she'd find out unless I told her.
But if it were as easy as that, I wouldn't be feeling all this pressure inside.
I don't know what's worse: telling a lie and being eaten alive by guilt, or drowning in shame for having told the truth.
(I guess my advice doesn't really solve his problem.)
You could just not go home for a while.
Think about it. You're in a taxi. I could take you as far away as you want.
Well, that'd make you a lot of money I'm sure, but it doesn't help solve my problem.
And here I thought you looked like the kind of guy I could trust.
(Looks like humor wasn't the right angle to go with...)
Here we are. Thank you for riding with Nagasu Taxi.
No, thank you for being such a good listener. I feel like a weight's been lifted off my shoulders. Here's the fare.
Take this tip as well. You've earned it!
Of course! Hope to see you around.
Thank you for riding with Nagasu Taxi. Here we are.

Thanks. Guess we've both got our issues, eh? But let's keep
battling on. Here's the fare.
Yeh-huh. See you around.
*sigh* Oh, right... I have to pay you, don't I?
Welp... Off to meet my doom... *groan*
(He doesn't look any happier than when he started. I guess I couldn't cheer him up.)
It's fine. Take me to <Color:22>Fukuhaku Street<Color:Default>, kiddo. Oops, guess you're not quite a kiddo anymore, are ya?
Aheheheh!
(I bet this guy's gonna talk my ear off.)
Please, get in.
I usually drive my own car, but tonight I'm going out drinkin', so I thought I'd take a taxi.
Pleased to be of service.
Well, aren't you a polite one? Heheh. How's business?
I have good days and bad days.
Oh, I read in the paper that they relaxed the regulations, and now there's too many taxis competing for too few passengers.
Must be hard making money as a taxi driver, eh?
I'd say it's just as hard in every industry.
Mm, suppose you're right. These days it's tough makin' a living no matter what you're doin'.
I gotta say, driver, I admire your broad perspective!
I try not to think about it much.
Yeah, worryin' about it can get ya down sometimes. I can understand that.
But this is your livelihood here, so ya oughta show at least a little interest. Otherwise the rug might get pulled out from under ya one day.
You're right. I hadn't considered that.
Hahaha, no need to change your opinion. I appreciate your honesty.
I'd rather be that than some wage-grubbing working stiff.
What? Was that a jab at me, driver?
Working for a corporation is no picnic, I can tell ya that. Everybody's got it rough these days.
...Sorry.
I guess sometimes it's hard to find customers in the taxi business.
It can be.
Then just when you think you've got a passenger, they only want to go a short way down the road.
That does happen, yes.
What goes through your head at times like that?
To be honest, I can't stand it when passengers do that.
Hahaha! Yeah, I figured. It's refreshing to hear from a straight-talker.
But I'm sure your customers feel bad enough for only taking a short fare in the first place.
Yeah, they know taxi drivers hate that. Next time try seeing it from their point of view.
I welcome any customer, even if they're going just a few blocks away.
Really? You don't secretly wish they'd take a longer trip?
Well, yes, at times.
But an empty cab earns nothing at all, so even short fares are a valuable source of income.
Hey, I like that attitude. Good on you!
I shortchange those lazy punks to make up for it.
Oh, uh... Hahah...
You know, as a professional, you really shouldn't joke about that.
I bet all sorts of people have been in this cab, eh, driver?
You got that right.
I imagine there've been a few you're not too fond of. Tell me, what sort of passenger gets on your nerves the most?
Ones that ask too many damn questions.
Ahaha, I can see how that⑬ Hey! Are you talking about me!?
And here I was, thinkin' we were having a nice chat. Turns out ya think I should just stop flappin' my gums!
(Uh-oh. That definitely pissed him off.)
I'd have to say anyone who's drunk.
Ah, right. People who've had a few too many tend to get unruly.
But, if you recall, I'm heading out for drinks right now.
I was thinking if you were a nice guy, I'd call you for the trip home, too.
But since you don't want a drunk in your taxi, I guess I should ask someone else.
(Damn. I went and made things awkward...)
Couples making out in the back seat.
Ahuhuhuh! Guess that means you're single, eh?
Come on, you can be honest!
You don't seem like such a bad guy to me. The right lady'll come along soon enough. And when she does⑬hoo boy. Enjoy what little freedom ya have left!
We're here. Thank you for choosing Nagasu Taxi.
Why, thank you for the pleasant trip! Here's the fare. I threw in a little tip as well.
I'll ask for you on the way back, too! See ya!
Pleasure's all mine. Thanks for the smooth trip. Here's what I owe ya.
Well, be seeing ya!
Ya know... I don't think you're cut out to be in the taxi business. Not till ya brush up on your people skills, at the very least.
I'm sorry if you didn't have a good experience.
Uh-huh... Well, I'll be tryin' somewhere else next time.
Hey. <Color:22>Nagasu Boulevard<Color:Default>, please.
Did you see that TV documentary on taxi drivers last night?
(I didn't catch it.)
Yeah!? It was pretty interesting, huh?
(Hm. I wonder what it was about.)
Yes, it was. I couldn't stop laughing.
What? But it wasn't funny. What was there to laugh about?
Are you sure you even saw it?
Sorry, I didn't.
Oh, come on. No need to lie just to make conversation.
Whatever. I'll tell you what it was about anyways.
A guy who used to be a company president went bankrupt and got a job as a taxi driver. He's only pulling in a little over 100,000 yen a month now.
That's not something I'm interested in.
Just thought I'd bring it up, seeing as you're a taxi driver and all.
Ain't no skin off my nose, but when you say you're not interested, you kinda kill the conversation.
(The passenger doesn't look pleased. I'd better think of something to say.)
Sorry about that. Can you tell me what it was about?
Huh? I thought you weren't interested. Well, I guess I'll tell you.
No, I must have missed it.
Oh, what am I thinking? You're probably way too busy with work to watch TV.
Could you tell me what it was about?
Sure, I'll give you the gist.
It was kind of sad to watch, actually.
They say that most taxi drivers are people who used to do other jobs. Is that true?
In a lot of cases, yes.
Does that apply to you?
Really? What job did you do before this? Were you a company president, too?
Not a president, but I was a chairman.
A chairman?
Hahaha! That's a good one, buddy!
Well, there's no way on earth a chairman could wind up as a taxi driver.
Maybe if you were chairman of the neighborhood watch! Ahahah!
(He took it as a joke, but at least he's happy.)
So, what was it you really did?
Something like the guy in that documentary.
You mean you really were a president? How big was the company you ran?
I did lead a lot of people, kind of like a president does.
Seriously!? That's just like the documentary!
Hmm. You do seem to carry yourself differently from other taxi drivers.
How big was the company you ran?
It was... big.
Wow! What was it called?
I'd prefer not to dwell on the past.
Oh, I see. Sorry about that, pal.
I bet you were a big shot, anyway. I can tell by the way you talk.
I won't ask why you became a driver, but hang in there, okay?
You'll get your time in the sun again. Just keep working hard! I'm rooting for you!
You shouldn't pry into other people's affairs.
I wouldn't call it prying. I just asked an innocent question.
Well, I'm not giving you an answer.
Aw, fine. I won't say another word.
(I think I made him angry.)
Don't just ignore me.
Fine, I've had enough! Forget I even asked!
(Looks like I made him mad.)
Thanks, that was a good ride! Here's the fare. I'll even give you a tip, too!
Keep your chin up, Mr. President!
Ah, thanks. Here's the fare.
You might've used to be a president, but you're a taxi driver now. You oughta learn the service trade a bit better.
Hmph. Goodbye.
That's the client whom you and Kiyokawa-kun went and apologized to after he complained. He mentioned he was ready for a rematch of some kind?
(That would be Crash Kajiwara, one of the Devil Killers' Four Kings. I'd better not lose today.)
Don't go, man! You're lucky you came back alive last time. This time you might not.
See you when I get back.
Hey! ...Wait for me!
What do you have for me?
Oh, right. Someone had a complaint about you, Suzuki-san. He was yelling over the phone, and he sounded really threatening. Any idea who that might be?
Your guess is as good as mine. Where should I go to make the apology?
Hang on a second... Here we go. Wouldn't you know it, he said he's at the highway rest area.
(The rest area... Another challenge from the Devil Killers, maybe?)
Come to think of it, you've been for a pickup at that rest area before. Maybe it's the same person.
Then he must be a regular. I'll go and clear things up.
Hey, guys!
Hello there, Kiyokawa-kun. Good timing. Suzuki-san is heading out to deal with a complaint. You should go along, too. You might learn something.
All right! Let's go, Suzuki-san!
No, I'd rather handle this on my own.
I don't see the harm in bringing him along. He needs to learn how to apologize properly from someone, might as well be you.
You said it, Hirakawa-san! Now let's hit the road!
(Great...)
Bahahah! Ready for another mauling, you prick? Sorry if you wind up dead!
That won't happen. Now let's get down to business.
Suzuki-san! You sure about this?

Don't worry, Kiyokawa. I'll make it back alive. You can
count on that.
Ahh... My old stomping grounds. Alas, the life of a street racer has already passed me by.
That wasn't all that long ago.
Heheh. Still felt good to say. Now, where's this complainer?
(I never should've brought this guy along to a race with the Devil Killers.)
So you're Suzuki from Nagasu Taxi, huh?
Dude! It's freakin' Kajiwara!
You know him or something?
Of course I do. He's a top racer in the Devil Killers. One of the Four Kings!
He drives like a maniac, and he's totaled more cars than you can count!
Worst of all, most cars he goes up against end up on the scrapheap. He's an absolute menace!

He's just as crazy when he's not behind the wheel, too.
He loves to pick fights, and he's put tons of people in the
hospital. You know what people call him?
Crash Kajiwara! Can you believe it!?
(At least he has a profile on some of these guys. That might come in handy.)
But what is Crash Kajiwara doing here? Unless...!?
Are you the one who called with the complaint?
Augh! A complaint from one of the Four Kings!? What the hell did you do, Suzuki-san!?
Two of my Devil Killers are in the hospital right now. They're messed up real bad. Got somethin' you wanna say?
I don't know what you're getting at. I did race some of your men, but none of them ended up injured. You sure you've got the right person?
Oh I'm damn sure, asshole!
Some punk-ass taxi driver takes on the Devil Killers in a race⑬and wins!? No fuckin' way I'm standing for that!
You beat two of the Devil Killers!?
Soon as I got the news, I lost it. Stomped 'em both into the floor! Shit was crazy.
So you put your own men in the hospital?
Yeah, and it's a cryin' shame. Two young guys with their whole lives ahead of 'em, now shattered to pieces. And it's all your goddamn fault!
So now you gotta deal with the first of the Four Kings, and I'm out for personal vengeance!
